Nothing changes in `casa-init`, `docs-check`, or the normative contract version (`CASA 1.10`).

## Consequences

- The public CASA Standard website automatically reflects every ADR, Spec, skill, and contract release merged to `main`, with zero duplicated normative prose.
- Any structural regression in site generation or internal links fails the PR gate before reaching GitHub Pages deployment.
- The built-in Markdown converter covers the syntax vocabulary used across this repository's documents; introducing new Markdown syntax outside that subset requires an explicit extension in `scripts/build-site` + a test case in `scripts/test-site`.

## Confirmation

```bash
scripts/test-site            # exit 0: deterministic build, intact links, SEO, and casa-init isolation
python3 scripts/docs-check   # exit 0: reference repo stays green with _site/ ignored
```

## Notes

Trigger: issue #37. Detailed behavior and edge cases in SPEC-0011.

SPEC-0001.title: casa-init installs and updates CASA infrastructure across any repository state
SPEC-0001.body:
# casa-init installs and updates CASA infrastructure across any repository state

## Objective

Anyone who wants to adopt CASA in a repository — empty, brand-new, legacy, or with pre-existing ADR/SDD docs — runs a single command and receives the complete infrastructure (validator, templates, router if absent, §3 gate) without any of the repository's own content being touched. Running it again updates the toolchain (it is also the update mechanism for already-onboarded repositories).

## Flow

```bash
scripts/casa-init <target> [--repo-id NAME] [--tier T0|T1]
```

1. Resolves the target directory (creating it if it does not exist), the contract's `casa-version`, and `casa-standard-ref` (short SHA of the source).
2. Copies the **toolchain** (tool-owned): `scripts/docs-check`, `scripts/pre-commit`, `docs/templates/*` — creates, updates when different, or reports `"up to date"` (`em dia`).
3. Handles **identity** (repo-owned): `AGENTS.md` is instantiated from the template only if absent (`repo-id`, `tier`, version, and ref stamped); if it already exists, only `casa-standard-ref` is updated — `casa-version` is the **repository's promise** (ADR-0010): inserted only when absent, never modified.
4. Installs the **gate** (ADR-0006): GitHub remote → CI workflow (from `docs/templates/docs-check.workflow.yml`, created if absent); no remote or remote on a host without a CI adapter → pre-commit hook (symlink to `scripts/pre-commit`), with a warning (`AVISO`) when a remote exists; no `.git` → prints guidance. (Evolved by SPEC-0009: effective repo-local hooks directory only, copy in worktrees, workflow targeting the actual default branch, and divergence warning.)
5. **Diagnoses**: runs the target's `docs-check` and reports findings — content migration is human work (§10), not this script's job.

## Contract

- Per-line output: `criado | atualizado | em dia | preservado | AVISO` (created | updated | up to date | preserved | WARNING) + path/reason.
- Exit 0 = installation completed; pending documentation migration is reported, not treated as a failure.
- Exit ≠ 0 only on usage errors (invalid target, target = `casa-standard` itself).
- **Never touches**: `docs/adr|specs|context`, `README`, `LICENSE`, source code, or an existing router (except `casa-standard-ref`, which belongs to the tool; `casa-version` is inserted only when absent — ADR-0010).

## Edge cases

| # | WHEN ⟨trigger⟩ | THE SYSTEM SHALL ⟨response⟩ |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the target directory does not exist | create it and proceed as a new repository |
| 2 | the target is `casa-standard` itself | abort with an error and exit ≠ 0 |
| 3 | `AGENTS.md` already exists in the target | preserve it; update only `casa-standard-ref`; insert `casa-version` only if absent |
| 4 | a toolchain file differs from the source | overwrite it and report `"updated"` (`atualizado`) |
| 5 | there is no `.git` in the target | skip gate installation and instruct the user to re-run after `git init` |
| 6 | `.git` exists with no remote | install the pre-commit hook (ADR-0006) |
| 7 | `.git` exists with a GitHub remote | create the CI workflow if absent; do not install the hook |
| 8 | `.git/hooks/pre-commit` exists and does not belong to CASA | leave it untouched and emit a warning (`AVISO`) |
| 9 | `docs-check` fails in the target after installation | keep exit 0 and report pending migration (§10) |
| 10 | run twice in a row with no changes in the source | alter zero bytes on the second run |
| 11 | `--repo-id` is omitted | derive it from the target directory's basename |
| 12 | `.git` exists with a remote on a host without a CI adapter (e.g., GitLab) | install the pre-commit hook and emit a warning (`AVISO`) instructing how to integrate `docs-check` into the host's CI (ADR-0006) |
| 13 | the existing router declares a `casa-version` different from the toolchain's | preserve the declaration (the repository's promise, ADR-0010) — the divergence is flagged by `docs-check`, not rewritten by `casa-init` |

## Open questions

(none — spec arrives decided)

## Definition of Done

```bash
scripts/test-casa-init        # exit 0 — all scenarios above green
python3 scripts/docs-check    # exit 0 — this repository stays green
```

## Human review

- Clarity of output messages for someone who has never seen CASA before.
- Migrating legacy content (status, frontmatter, deduplication) remains a human decision — the script only diagnoses; verify that it never crosses that line.

## Verification

```text
2026-06-09 · scripts/test-casa-init → 16 PASS / 0 FAIL (EARS 1–11 covered), exit 0
2026-06-09 · python3 scripts/docs-check → 5 docs · 0 error(s) · 0 warning(s), exit 0
2026-06-12 · scripts/test-casa-init → 19 PASS / 0 FAIL (EARS 1–12 covered; per-host gate, ADR-0006), exit 0
2026-06-12 · python3 scripts/docs-check → 8 docs · 0 error(s) · 0 warning(s), exit 0
2026-06-13 · bash scripts/test-casa-init → 23 PASS / 0 FAIL (casa-version + regressions), exit 0
2026-06-13 · python3 scripts/docs-check → 10 docs · 0 error(s) · 0 warning(s), exit 0
2026-07-05 · bash scripts/test-casa-init → 31 PASS / 0 FAIL (EARS-13: existing casa-version preserved; casa-standard-ref updated; casa-init/docs-check constants synchronized — ADR-0010), exit 0
```

SPEC-0002.title: install.sh bootstraps CASA via curl|sh without cloning or introducing a second source of truth
SPEC-0002.body:
# install.sh bootstraps CASA via curl|sh without cloning or introducing a second source of truth

> Shared conventions: this repository has no `docs/context/CONVENTIONS.md`; the ownership
> contract (toolchain × identity × content) is defined in SPEC-0001 and is not repeated here.

## Objective

Anyone who wants to apply CASA runs **a single command, without cloning anything**:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/atplus-digital/casa-standard/main/install.sh | sh -s -- <target> [--repo-id NAME] [--tier T0|T1]
```

The script downloads the `casa-standard` tarball (pinnable ref), extracts it into a temporary directory, and executes `scripts/casa-init` from there — all bootstrap semantics remain in SPEC-0001; this spec covers transport only.

## Flow

1. Validates prerequisites (`python3`, `tar`; `curl` only when downloading) — fails clearly **before** downloading or writing anything.
2. Resolves the source: `CASA_TARBALL` (local tarball, offline) or download from `codeload.github.com/<repo>/tar.gz/<ref>` (`CASA_REF`, default `main`).
3. Extracts into `mktemp -d` (cleaned up via `trap` on any exit) and detects the root directory — `codeload` tarballs have a top-level prefix directory; flat tarballs do not.
4. Resolves the stamp: pinned ref, or short SHA of `main` via `git ls-remote` when available; exports `CASA_STANDARD_REF` and executes `casa-init` forwarding all arguments intact (no arguments or flags only → target defaults to the current directory).

## Contract

- Entire body wrapped in `main()`, invoked on the very last line (`main "$@"`) — a truncated download executes nothing.
- Writes only inside `mktemp` and the target directory (via `casa-init`); no `sudo`, nothing written to `$HOME`.
- POSIX `sh` (no bashisms); exit ≠ 0 with a `casa-install: ...` message on any failure.
- Environment variables: `CASA_REF` (ref to download/stamp), `CASA_REPO` (repository override), `CASA_TARBALL` (local tarball source; stamp becomes `CASA_REF` or `local`).

## Edge cases

| # | WHEN ⟨trigger⟩ | THE SYSTEM SHALL ⟨response⟩ |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | executed with no arguments | run `casa-init` against the current working directory |
| 2 | executed with target and flags | forward them intact to `casa-init` |
| 3 | executed with flags only (no positional target) | treat the current working directory as the target |
| 4 | `python3` is unavailable | fail with a clear message before downloading and without writing anything |
| 5 | download is truncated or interrupted | execute nothing (structural `main()` guard) |
| 6 | `CASA_REF` points to a tag or SHA | download that ref and stamp it into the target's router |
| 7 | `CASA_TARBALL` points to a local tarball | use the local tarball without touching the network |
| 8 | tarball has a prefix directory (`codeload`) or is flat | detect the root directory in both archive layouts |
| 9 | termination on success, failure, or signal interruption | remove the temporary directory (`trap`) |

## Open questions

(none — spec arrives decided)

## Definition of Done

```bash
scripts/test-install          # exit 0 — scenarios above green, offline
python3 scripts/docs-check    # exit 0 — this repository stays green
```

## Human review

- `curl|sh` security posture: is the script still auditable in ~30 seconds? Is its write scope still strictly `mktemp` + target?
- EARS-9 (`trap` removes the temporary directory) is verified by inspection — there is no automated assertion for signal trapping.
- `README.md` preserves the two-step path (download, inspect, run) for users who do not trust piping into `sh`.

## Verification

```text
2026-06-09 · scripts/test-install → 11 PASS / 0 FAIL (EARS 1–8 covered; EARS-9 by inspection), exit 0
2026-06-09 · scripts/test-casa-init → 16 PASS / 0 FAIL (SPEC-0001 regression), exit 0
2026-06-09 · python3 scripts/docs-check → 7 docs · 0 error(s) · 0 warning(s), exit 0
2026-06-13 · bash scripts/test-install → 11 PASS / 0 FAIL (regression with CASA 1.1), exit 0
```

SPEC-0003.title: docs-check validates the core invariants of the CASA 1.1 contract
SPEC-0003.body:
# docs-check validates the core invariants of the CASA 1.1 contract

## Objective

`docs-check` goes beyond validating only the ADR/Spec layer and begins enforcing the core invariants of the CASA contract: an intact router, finalized Specs free of structural loose ends, real implementation paths, and accepted-ADR immutability in CI.

## Flow

```bash
python3 scripts/docs-check [--root .] [--emit-index] [--warn-only]
python3 scripts/docs-check --check-adr-immutability --base-ref origin/main
```

1. Validates the router (`AGENTS.md`) before the docs: CASA metadata, global DoD, and context pointers.
2. Validates ADRs/Specs as before: frontmatter, dependency graph, statuses, generated indexes, and repository hygiene.
3. Enforces strict Spec rules when `status` is `accepted` or `implemented`.
4. When `--check-adr-immutability` is passed (evolved by SPEC-0009: matched by ADR number against the merge-base, forbidding deletion and status regression), compares modified ADRs against `--base-ref` and rejects any body edit to an ADR that was already `accepted`, `superseded`, or `deprecated`.

## Contract

- `AGENTS.md` is mandatory and must declare `casa-repo-id`, `casa-tier`, `casa-version`, and `casa-standard-ref` inside a `yaml` code block.
- The router's global DoD must exist and contain at least one executable command line inside a fenced code block.
- Every `docs/context/*.md` pointer declared in the context map must exist on disk.
- An `accepted` or `implemented` Spec must not leave any unchecked `- [ ]` item under `## Open questions` (`## Questões em aberto`).
- An `accepted` or `implemented` Spec must have a DoD containing a real executable command with no placeholders.
- An `implemented` Spec must have a non-empty `implemented-by` list without placeholders, where every path resolves to an existing file or directory in the repository.
- The immutability lint allows newly added ADRs as well as changes limited to frontmatter or the top `VERDADE ATUAL` (current-truth) callout; modifying the body of an already-accepted ADR is an error.

## Edge cases

| # | WHEN ⟨trigger⟩ | THE SYSTEM SHALL ⟨response⟩ |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | brand-new repository bootstrapped by `casa-init` | pass `docs-check` without requiring dummy context chapters |
| 2 | router omits `casa-version` | fail pointing out the missing metadata field |
| 3 | router points to a non-existent `docs/context/INFRA.md` | fail pointing out the broken pointer |
| 4 | an `accepted` Spec keeps `- [ ]` in open questions | fail because the Spec did not arrive decided |
| 5 | an `accepted` Spec keeps `<placeholder>` in its DoD | fail because the DoD is not executable |
| 6 | an `implemented` Spec lists a non-existent path in `implemented-by` | fail pointing out the missing path |
| 7 | an accepted ADR has its body modified under `--check-adr-immutability` | fail reporting an immutability violation |
| 8 | an accepted ADR only gains a `VERDADE ATUAL` callout and supersession frontmatter | pass the immutability lint |

## Open questions

(none — spec arrives decided)

## Definition of Done

```bash
bash scripts/test-docs-check        # exit 0 — scenarios above green
python3 scripts/docs-check          # exit 0 — this repository stays green
```

## Human review

- Do error messages help an adopter fix their router or Spec without reading validator source code?
- Does the immutability lint stay simple enough not to turn into opaque policy?

# docs-check recognizes the TESTS chapter declared in the router and requires a canonical command

> Shared conventions: `STANDARD.md` §4 (context chapters) and §8 (what CI validates).
> This spec does not repeat them — it only defines the behavior of the first recognized
> chapter in the closed registry introduced by ADR-0008.

## Objective

Declaring `docs/context/TESTS.md` in the router's Context map no longer checks merely that the file exists — it ensures the chapter fulfills its purpose: listing at least one canonical test command. The trigger is the **router declaration**; the rule lives inside `docs-check` (closed registry `RECOGNIZED_CHAPTERS`), never in the adopting repository.

## Flow

1. `validate_router` extracts all `docs/context/*.md` pointers referenced in the router (pre-existing rule: each target must exist).
2. For every pointer whose file exists and belongs to the closed registry of recognized chapters, `docs-check` enforces that capability's content invariant.
3. `TESTS` capability (`docs/context/TESTS.md`): requires at least one executable line inside a fenced code block (using the same `executable_lines` criterion applied to the global DoD).

## Contract

- The set of recognized chapters is **closed** (`RECOGNIZED_CHAPTERS`) and lives in `docs-check`; extending it requires an ADR in `casa-standard` (ADR-0008).
- The trigger is declaring the pointer in the router, never the mere physical presence of the file on disk.
- Any **unrecognized** chapter declared in the router remains subject only to the file-existence rule.
- The `TESTS` capability fails the gate when the declared chapter contains no command in a code block; the error message names the recognized chapter and instructs the user either to add the canonical command or to remove the pointer.
- The template `docs/templates/context.TESTS.template.md` is distributed by `casa-init`.

## Edge cases

| # | WHEN ⟨trigger⟩ | THE SYSTEM SHALL ⟨response⟩ |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | router declares `TESTS.md` and the chapter contains a canonical command | pass (`test-docs-check` EARS-9) |
| 2 | router declares `TESTS.md` and the chapter contains prose only | fail pointing out the recognized chapter (EARS-10) |
| 3 | router declares `TESTS.md` but the file does not exist | fail as a broken pointer (pre-existing rule, EARS-3) |
| 4 | router declares an UNRECOGNIZED chapter (`INFRA.md`) with no command | pass — the closed registry only requires existence for unrecognized chapters (EARS-11) |
| 5 | new repository created by `casa-init` with no declared chapters | pass without requiring dummy chapters (EARS-1) |

SPEC-0005.body:
# casa-init ensures the CLAUDE.md bridge to the router in every adopting repository

## Objective

Every repository with CASA installed is readable by Claude Code with zero manual setup: `casa-init` ensures a `CLAUDE.md` whose first non-comment line imports the router (`@AGENTS.md`). The router remains the single source of truth (ADR-0009).

## Flow

1. After handling router identity (SPEC-0001, step 3), `casa-init` inspects `CLAUDE.md` in the target repository.
2. Absent → creates it from `docs/templates/CLAUDE.template.md` and reports `criado` (created).
3. Present and containing `@AGENTS.md` → reports `em dia` (up to date); zero bytes change.
4. Present without `@AGENTS.md` → preserved byte-for-byte; emits `AVISO` (WARNING) instructing the user to add the import line.

## Contract

- The target's `CLAUDE.md` is **repository identity**: `casa-init` never overwrites or edits it — not even to inject the import (unlike the router, whose tool-owned metadata is updated; in the bridge file nothing is tool-owned after initial creation).
- `docs/templates/CLAUDE.template.md` is **toolchain**: distributed and updated inside the adopter's `docs/templates/` alongside the other official templates.
- Output follows the vocabulary established in SPEC-0001: `criado | em dia | AVISO` (created | up to date | WARNING).
- Applies to both T0 and T1 — every repository with a router.

## Edge cases

| # | WHEN ⟨trigger⟩ | THE SYSTEM SHALL ⟨response⟩ |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `CLAUDE.md` does not exist in the target | create it from the template with `@AGENTS.md` present |
| 2 | `CLAUDE.md` exists and contains `@AGENTS.md` | alter zero bytes and report `em dia` (up to date) |
| 3 | `CLAUDE.md` exists without `@AGENTS.md` | alter zero bytes and emit `AVISO` (WARNING) |
| 4 | run twice in a row with no changes in the source | alter zero bytes on the second run (EARS-10 of SPEC-0001 covers the bridge) |

SPEC-0006.body:
# docs-check surfaces maintenance warnings: contract version coherence and backlog location

## Objective

The gate begins **informing** (without blocking) about two maintenance drifts that previously aged in silence: a contract declaration (`casa-version`) out of sync with the installed toolchain (ADR-0010) and a backlog file placed in the wrong directory (`docs/context/`, ADR-0011).

## Flow

1. During router validation, if `casa-version` has a valid format, `docs-check` compares `(major, minor)` of the declared version against `CONTRACT_VERSION` (a constant inside `docs-check` itself) and emits a warning on mismatch — the message direction depends on which side is behind.
2. After router validation, `docs-check` lists `docs/context/` (if present) and emits a warning for any file whose lowercase name is `backlog.md`.
3. Warnings are emitted on the standard warning channel (`AVISO:`) and **do not affect the exit code**.

## Contract

- `CONTRACT_VERSION` in `docs-check` = the CASA contract version implemented by the toolchain; it must match `CASA_VERSION` in `casa-init` from the same snapshot — synchronization is enforced by a test scenario in `casa-standard` CI (`test-casa-init`).
- Version comparison uses `(major, minor)`; patch components do not trigger warnings.
- Location checking matches filenames via directory listing (deterministic across both case-sensitive and case-insensitive filesystems), never via `exists()`.

## Edge cases

| # | WHEN ⟨trigger⟩ | THE SYSTEM SHALL ⟨response⟩ |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the router declares a `casa-version` lower than `CONTRACT_VERSION` | warn that the declared contract is behind: read the `casa-standard` CHANGELOG and bump the declaration once the repository satisfies the newer contract |
| 2 | the router declares a `casa-version` higher than `CONTRACT_VERSION` | warn that the toolchain is behind: run `scripts/casa-init` from a current snapshot |
| 3 | declared version and `CONTRACT_VERSION` match on `(major, minor)` | emit no version warning |
| 4 | `casa-version` has an invalid format | emit only the existing format error — do not stack a coherence warning on top |
| 5 | a `backlog.md` file (in any casing) exists inside `docs/context/` | warn about location: move it to `docs/BACKLOG.md` and update router pointers |
| 6 | `docs/BACKLOG.md` sits at the root of `docs/` (the right place) | emit no location warning |

SPEC-0007.title: docs-reserve reserves the next NNNN number and scaffolds the document from its template
SPEC-0007.body:
# docs-reserve reserves the next NNNN number and scaffolds the document from its template

## Objective

Reserving a number and scaffolding a new ADR or Spec becomes a single-command operation — sequential number computed from actual repository state (files on disk + ledger), document instantiated from the official template with today's date and the right H1, and reservation recorded in the ledger — eliminating manual numbering mistakes that cause collisions and cascading renumbering (issue #12).

## Flow

```bash
scripts/docs-reserve adr  "decision title"   [--dry-run] [--no-emit-index]
scripts/docs-reserve spec "behavior title"   [--dry-run] [--no-emit-index]
```

1. Refuses to run if a backlog file lives inside `docs/context/` while `docs/BACKLOG.md` is absent (ADR-0011).
2. Collects allocated numbers: `NNNN-*.md` files in the target layer + rows in the matching ledger section (`## Reservas ADR` / `## Reservas Spec`); any unparseable row inside that section is explicitly FLAGGED.
3. Next number = `max + 1`; gaps are noted (never reused).
4. Creates `docs/<layer>/NNNN-slug.md` from the repository's template: today's `date`, H1 = title, and the template's default status (`proposed` / `draft`).
5. Appends `| NNNN | title | date | em uso |` to the section's table (creating the ledger file or section if absent) and regenerates indexes via `docs-check --emit-index` (unless `--no-emit-index` is passed).

## Contract

- Output: `Reserved <ID>` + `Created <path>` + `Updated docs/BACKLOG.md` + instruction to run `docs-check` (which remains the sole validation authority — ADR-0002).
- Never overwrites an existing file; exit ≠ 0 only on usage errors (invalid layer, title yielding an empty slug, missing template, backlog in the wrong directory).
- Table parser: first cell matches `NNNN` or `ADR-NNNN` / `SPEC-NNNN`; remaining cells are free-form. Any non-matching line inside the reservation section triggers a warning (`AVISO`) quoting the offending line while execution continues.
- `--dry-run` prints the computed number, target path, and ledger row without writing **anything**.
- Coordination across parallel worktrees/branches is out of scope (ADR-0013) — the safeguard is the textual merge conflict on the reservation table.

## Edge cases

| # | WHEN ⟨trigger⟩ | THE SYSTEM SHALL ⟨response⟩ |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | freshly bootstrapped repository with no ledger | reserve `0001`, create the doc from its template (today's date, H1 = title), and create `docs/BACKLOG.md` with the reservation table |
| 2 | reservations across both layers | number each layer independently and sequentially |
| 3 | manual row in the table has a number higher than the max file on disk | honor it (`max(files, reservations) + 1`) and note any gaps |
| 3b | row uses a prefixed ID format (`ADR-0004`) | count it normally (backward compatibility with existing ledgers) |
| 4 | unparseable line inside the reservations section | emit a warning (`AVISO`) quoting the line and continue — never ignore silently |
| 5 | backlog sits in `docs/context/` with no `docs/BACKLOG.md` | abort with an error citing ADR-0011 and write nothing |
| 6 | title contains accents or punctuation | transliterate into an ASCII kebab-case slug |
| 7 | `--dry-run` is passed | print number, file path, and table row without writing anything |
| 8 | title transliterates to an empty slug | fail with a clear error |
| 9 | reservation completes | leave the repository passing `docs-check` (indexes regenerated automatically) |

## Open questions

(none — spec arrives decided)

## Definition of Done

```bash
bash scripts/test-docs-reserve   # exit 0 — cases 1–9 above green
python3 scripts/docs-check       # exit 0 — this repository stays green
```

## Human review

- Error and warning messages are actionable for someone who has never read ADR-0013 (they explain what to do next).
- This repository's migrated ledger remains clean and readable for humans.

SPEC-0008.title: casa-update-check maintains an issue-tracker notice when the declared CASA contract falls behind
SPEC-0008.body:
# casa-update-check maintains an issue-tracker notice when the declared CASA contract falls behind

## Objective

An adopting repository with a GitHub remote discovers automatically, once a week, when its declared CASA contract version has fallen behind the current release — surfaced as **a single actionable issue** in its own tracker that never duplicates and closes itself once the repository catches up. None of this touches the gate.

## Flow

1. The scheduled workflow (`casa-update-check.yml`: weekly cron + `workflow_dispatch`) runs `sh scripts/casa-update-check` using the repository's `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`issues: write`).
2. The script reads `casa-version` from `AGENTS.md` and the latest contract version from the first `## CASA X.Y` heading in `casa-standard`'s raw `CHANGELOG.md` (URL overridable via `CASA_SOURCE_URL` for testing and forks).
3. Compares version order: **behind** → ensures the `casa-update` label exists and opens the notice issue, or **edits** the existing open one in place (updating title and body to the current versions). **Up to date / ahead** → closes any open `casa-update` issue with a comment.
4. Issue body instructs the maintainer to run `casa-init` (or `install.sh`), review the CHANGELOG entries between the two versions, and bump `casa-version` once the repository complies (ADR-0010).

## Contract

- **Always exits 0** when external conditions fail: network unreachable, unreadable CHANGELOG, missing or malformed `casa-version` — logs and exits cleanly; enforcing router integrity belongs to `docs-check`, and a scheduled background job must never turn into a noisy red failure.
- Exit ≠ 0 only on usage errors (non-existent root path).
- At most **one** open `casa-update` issue per repository at any time.
- Installation (`casa-init`): GitHub remote → workflow created if absent, preserved if already present; no GitHub remote → not installed (Appendix A.5). The workflow template is toolchain-owned (updated in `docs/templates/`); the installed workflow in `.github/workflows/` is repo-owned.

## Edge cases

| # | WHEN ⟨trigger⟩ | THE SYSTEM SHALL ⟨response⟩ |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | declared contract is behind the current version | open an issue labeled `casa-update` (title naming both versions) |
| 2 | an open `casa-update` issue already exists | edit it in place — never open a duplicate |
| 3 | declared contract matches the current version | open nothing, and close any open `casa-update` issue if present |
| 4 | declared contract is ahead of the current version | treat as up to date (policing version validity is not this job's role) |
| 5 | network or upstream URL is unreachable | exit 0 with a log message — never fail the workflow job |
| 6 | `casa-version` is unreadable in the router | exit 0 with a log message — router validation belongs to `docs-check` |
| 7 | target repository has no GitHub remote | do not install the workflow at all (`casa-init`, ADR-0006 / ADR-0016) |
| 8 | workflow file already exists in the target | preserve it untouched (`casa-init` treats installed workflows as repo-owned) |

## Open questions

(none — spec arrives decided)

## Definition of Done

```bash
bash scripts/test-update-check   # exit 0 — cases 1–6 with curl/gh stubs green
bash scripts/test-casa-init      # exit 0 — cases 7–8 (per-host installation) green
python3 scripts/docs-check       # exit 0 — this repository stays green
```

## Human review

- Generated issue copy is self-sufficient for someone who has never read the ADRs (states clearly what to run and in what order).
- Weekly cron schedule (staggered off-peak time) is reasonable across the repository fleet.

## Verification


SPEC-0009.title: Reliable gate: hook, CI, and immutability validate what actually lands
SPEC-0009.body:
# Reliable gate: hook, CI, and immutability validate what actually lands

## Objective

The CASA gate stops turning green on false guarantees. The 2026-11-18 audit (internal review + consolidated CASA × atplus report) reproduced, in disposable test repositories, scenarios where `docs-check`, the pre-commit hook, the CI workflow, or `casa-init` approved changes forbidden by `STANDARD.md` — or installed a gate that Git never actually executes. This spec closes all of those gaps in a **backward-compatible** release (CASA 1.9): for the most part, the toolchain now enforces what §5 and §8 already promised; the handful of net-new prohibitions are listed under Contract. A three-lens independent review (code, adopters, normative coherence) over the first iteration of this delivery added edge cases 22–30.

## Flow

1. `casa-init` installs the gate where Git actually executes it — or skips installation and explains why.
2. At commit time, the pre-commit hook validates the **Git index** (`docs-check --staged`).
3. In CI, the workflow compares against the event's true base (PR: target branch; push: previous commit), and the immutability lint compares every immutable ADR **by number** against the merge-base.
4. `docs-check` applies the same HTML-comment and placeholder rules to the router and `TESTS.md` that it already enforced on Specs.

## Contract

- CASA 1.9 (compatible). Generated index format and existing CLI flags remain unchanged; new flag: `--staged` (mutually exclusive with `--emit-index` and `--check-adr-immutability`).
- New errors where `STANDARD.md` already forbade the state: duplicate frontmatter keys (§6), broken context pointer inside a Markdown link and DoD present only inside HTML comments (§8.1), empty or list-typed `status` (§8.2), and ADR body altered via file rename or deletion (§5.1).
- Net-new prohibitions: ADR status regression is an **error** — it fires only on a PR that regresses status, never on an idle repository; an unquoted `<placeholder>` in the global DoD or `TESTS.md` and self-referential `builds-on` are **warnings** during the 1.9 adoption window. Additional new warnings: legacy template `npm` example DoD; top `VERDADE ATUAL` callout exceeding 3 lines.
- An existing workflow in an adopter repository is never overwritten; divergence from the current template emits a warning (`AVISO`).
- `--staged` reads the exact tree the commit would record; only the router and `docs/` load blob contents while all other tracked paths are read as names only — runtime does not grow with total repository file count.

## Edge cases

| # | WHEN ⟨trigger⟩ | THE SYSTEM SHALL ⟨response⟩ |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `casa-init` creates a new router | put `python3 scripts/docs-check` in the global DoD, never a dummy example command |
| 2 | global DoD still has the old template's `npm` example | warn (exit 0) prompting replacement with real repository commands |
| 3 | global DoD or declared `TESTS.md` only has commands inside HTML comments | fail |
| 4 | global DoD has a bare `<placeholder>` / Spec DoD has quoted `"<Tag>"` or shell redirection `<in >out` | warn (1.9 window) / pass |
| 5 | Context map points to a non-existent chapter via Markdown link | fail just like a backtick-quoted pointer |
| 6 | frontmatter has a duplicate key, `status: ""`, or `status: [x]` | fail with a clean diagnostic message; never crash with a traceback (including under `--warn-only`) |
| 7 | `builds-on` references the document itself | warn (1.9 window) |
| 8 | immutable ADR is renamed with body edits / renamed without body edits | fail citing the old path / pass |
| 9 | immutable ADR is deleted | fail |
| 10 | immutable ADR status regresses (`accepted` → `proposed`) | fail |
| 11 | `VERDADE ATUAL` quote appears mid-body / newly added top callout exceeds 3 lines | treat mid-body quote as body edit (fail) / fail |
| 12 | feature branch is behind a base branch that gained a new accepted ADR | pass — comparison runs against the merge-base |
| 13 | `.DS_Store` ignored by `.gitignore` / unignored duplicate `x 2.md` | pass / fail |
| 14 | doc is invalid in the index and fixed only on disk / valid in the index and broken on disk | `--staged` fails / passes |
| 15 | repository configures a repo-local `core.hooksPath` | install the hook into the configured hooks directory |
| 16 | `casa-init` runs inside a Git worktree | install the hook into the common hooks directory as a standalone copy; checkouts without the toolchain are not blocked |
| 17 | target is a subdirectory inside another Git repository | do not install a gate in the parent repository; warn; parent commits remain unaffected |
| 18 | GitHub remote uses default branch `master`; existing workflow diverges from template | render `branches: [master]`, event base comparison, and required-check note; emit `AVISO` without overwriting an existing workflow |
| 19 | `docs-reserve spec` runs | write title into the body's H1 while keeping frontmatter comments intact (restores SPEC-0007) |
| 20 | `casa-update-check` cannot query issues / is invoked from another working directory | do not open an issue blindly, log and exit 0 / operate on the specified root |
| 21 | pinned installation via pipe | documentation passes `CASA_REF` to `sh`, not to `curl` |
| 22 | checkout has an older `docs-check` predating `--staged` (worktree on an older branch) | fall back to running that validator in disk mode — never block every commit |
| 23 | `core.hooksPath` points outside the repository (global hook configuration) | do not install the hook; emit a warning |
| 24 | existing hook is a copy or symlink from an earlier CASA version | update it (`"atualizado"`); foreign hooks remain untouched |
| 25 | `--staged` runs with symlinked `AGENTS.md`, sparse-checkout excluding `docs/`, or `git add -N` | validate what the commit would actually record: symlink resolved, sparse-checkout unaffected, intent-to-add (`add -N`) excluded |
| 26 | `implemented-by` points to a path present only in the index / only on disk | `--staged` passes / fails |
| 27 | top `VERDADE ATUAL` callout > 3 lines already existed in the base | untouched: pass; edited without shrinking to ≤ 3 lines: fail; shrunk to ≤ 3 lines: pass |
| 28 | `VERDADE ATUAL` marker repeated across consecutive lines to stretch the callout | count as a single callout block (fail above 3 lines) |
| 29 | published repository lacks `origin/HEAD` and has a single remote branch (`develop`) | render `branches: [develop]` in the generated workflow |
| 30 | CI workflow template | also trigger on `merge_group` (merge queue), comparing against the merge group's base |

## Out of scope

- Requiring `## Confirmação` (`## Confirmation`) on accepted ADRs, cycle detection in `builds-on`, and escaping `|` in titles inside generated READMEs (which would dirty generated indexes across all adopters) — recorded separately for dedicated decisions.
- Adoption window with ratchet (issue #19): separate decision.
- Making required branch-protection status checks a formal T1 contract requirement (contract change → requires its own ADR); here `casa-init` and migration notes provide guidance only.
- The `## Confirmação` sections of ADR-0001 and ADR-0006 inspect `.git/hooks/pre-commit` directly and yield false negatives under `core.hooksPath` or worktrees; accepted ADR bodies are immutable — left for whichever future ADR supersedes them.

## Open questions

(none — spec arrives decided)

## Definition of Done

```bash
bash scripts/test-docs-check    # exit 0 — cases 2–14, 25–28
scripts/test-casa-init          # exit 0 — cases 1, 15–18, 22–24, 29–30
scripts/test-docs-reserve       # exit 0 — case 19
scripts/test-update-check       # exit 0 — case 20
scripts/test-install            # exit 0 — case 21
python3 scripts/docs-check      # exit 0 — this repository stays green
```

## Human review

- Are the new diagnostic messages (rename, status regression, `--staged`) clear enough for an adopter to fix issues without reading validator code?
- Is the divergent-workflow warning (`AVISO`) helpful, or does it become noise for adopters who intentionally customized their workflow file?

# casa-init distributes the casa-* delivery-cycle skills

## Objective

Every T1 repository bootstrapped or updated by `casa-init` receives the §9 delivery cycle as agent-executable skills (`casa-explore`, `casa-propose`, `casa-apply`, `casa-verify`, `casa-close`) in the open Agent Skills format, discoverable both by clients following the `.agents/skills/` convention and by Claude Code (ADR-0017).

## Flow

1. The single source of truth for skills is `docs/templates/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` in `casa-standard`.
2. `casa-init` reads the repository tier from the router (falling back to `--tier` on legacy routers missing the key); in T1 repositories, it renders and copies each skill into both `.agents/skills/<name>/` and `.claude/skills/<name>/` in the target — creating, updating on drift, or reporting `"up to date"` (`em dia`). In T0 repositories, it installs none and removes any of our `casa-*` skills left over from an earlier run.
3. The adopter's agent discovers skills via their `description`; users can also invoke them directly by name.

## Contract

- Skill frontmatter contains only portable fields (`name`, `description`); `name` matches the parent directory name.
- `casa-*` skills belong to the toolchain; skills under any other name in the skill directories belong to the repository.
- The `STANDARD.md` link inside rendered skills tracks the toolchain snapshot (`casa-standard-ref`), keeping `blob/main/` when `ref` is `local` or `unknown`; `STANDARD.md` itself is never copied into adopting repositories.
- Nothing changes in `docs-check`: skills are workflow guidance, not a gate (ADR-0017).

## Edge cases

| # | WHEN ⟨trigger⟩ | THE SYSTEM SHALL ⟨response⟩ |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `casa-init` runs on a T1 repository | install all five skills into both `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` |
| 2 | skills are installed | make them byte-for-byte identical across both directories and equal to the rendered template (LF line endings preserved) |
| 3 | skill template exists in `casa-standard` | carry valid, portable Agent Skills frontmatter (two fields, `name` = directory, `description` 1–1024 chars with no `<` or `>`) |
| 4 | a skill references `scripts/…` | ensure that script exists in the toolchain installed in the target |
| 5 | an adopter edits a `casa-*` skill / repo has its own differently named skill | restore `casa-*` to the rendered template reporting `"updated"` (`atualizado`) / leave the repo's own skill untouched |
| 6 | `casa-init` runs on a T0 repository (new, legacy with `--tier T0`, quoted `casa-tier`, or downgraded from T1) | install no skills (and remove our `casa-*` skills if present), reporting the reason |
| 7 | second consecutive run with no source changes | alter zero bytes (idempotence, EARS-10 of SPEC-0001) |
| 8 | skill installed with a Git ref / with ref `local` or `unknown` | point `STANDARD.md` links to the `casa-standard-ref` stamped in the router / keep `blob/main/` |
| 9 | `.claude` is a regular file | emit a warning without a traceback; still install the gate and `.agents/skills/` |
| 10 | a skills directory is ignored by `.gitignore` | warn that the installed skills will remain local to this machine |
| 11 | skill is listed in retired skills / homonymous skill (valid or non-UTF-8) not authored by CASA | remove if carrying the CASA marker / preserve without error |
| 12 | a skill template cites `§N` or `§N.M` | ensure that section or subsection exists in `STANDARD.md` |

## Definition of Done

```bash
scripts/test-casa-init        # exit 0 — cases 1–6 and 8–12 (SPEC-0010/N) plus case 7 (EARS-10)
python3 scripts/docs-check    # exit 0 — this repository stays green
```

## Human review

- Do the skill descriptions trigger the right skill in the agents used at atplus (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) without false-positive activations?
- Does every skill stay strictly within what `STANDARD.md` already specifies, introducing no hidden rules?

SPEC-0011.title: build-site generates the CASA Standard static website for GitHub Pages
SPEC-0011.body:
# build-site generates the CASA Standard static website for GitHub Pages

## Objective

Publish at `https://atplus-digital.github.io/casa-standard/` (and support identical local inspection) a complete static website for the CASA Standard — editorial overview with copyable quickstart, navigable `STANDARD.md`, interactive ADR and Spec graph explorer, `casa-*` skills catalog, and `CHANGELOG.md` release history — compiled directly from the repository's canonical sources, with zero content duplication and zero external dependencies (ADR-0018).

## Flow

1. Developer or CI runs `python3 scripts/build-site [--root .] [--out _site] [--base-url URL]`.
2. The script reads `STANDARD.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/index.json`, `docs/adr/*.md`, `docs/specs/*.md`, and `docs/templates/skills/*/SKILL.md`, computes forward and reverse graph edges (`builds-on`, `superseded-by`, `cited by`), and renders semantic static HTML into `_site/`, copying `site/{style.css,app.js,favicon.svg}` to `_site/assets/` and emitting `_site/assets/search-index.json` plus `_site/.nojekyll`.
3. On PRs and pushes, `scripts/test-site` validates site generation in the gate; on pushes to `main` (or `workflow_dispatch`), `.github/workflows/pages.yml` deploys `_site/` to GitHub Pages via `actions/deploy-pages`.

## Contract

- **Canonical inputs:** `STANDARD.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/index.json`, `docs/adr/*.md`, `docs/specs/*.md`, `docs/templates/skills/*/SKILL.md`, and presentation assets in `site/`.
- **Routes generated under `_site/`:**
  - `index.html` — editorial landing page, the 4 pillars, interactive repository anatomy, the 5-skill `casa-*` delivery cycle, quickstart with copyable commands, and live repository metrics;
  - `standard/index.html` — full `STANDARD.md` with sticky sidebar table of contents, stable section anchors, and clickable `ADR-NNNN` / `SPEC-NNNN` cross-references;
  - `grafo/index.html` — interactive SVG causal graph + table filterable by layer, status, and full-text query;
  - `adr/<slug>/index.html` and `specs/<slug>/index.html` — dedicated page for every document in `docs/index.json`, displaying derived metadata, upstream links (`builds-on`), downstream backlinks (`cited by` / `citado por`), `implemented-by`, and a highlighted `VERDADE ATUAL` callout on superseded ADRs;
  - `skills/index.html` — catalog of `casa-*` Agent Skills showing live description character-budget meters and full skill bodies;
  - `changelog/index.html` — contract version history parsed from `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Relative links:** all internal `href` and `src` attributes use paths relative to the current page's depth, working seamlessly both under `/casa-standard/` on GitHub Pages and from a local root directory.
- **Isolation:** `scripts/build-site`, `scripts/test-site`, and `site/` are never copied by `casa-init`; `_site/` is ignored via `.gitignore`.

## Edge cases

| # | WHEN ⟨trigger⟩ | THE SYSTEM SHALL ⟨response⟩ |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `scripts/build-site` runs against the repository | generate all primary routes, one page per entry in `docs/index.json`, `assets/search-index.json`, and `.nojekyll`, exiting 0 |
| 2 | the version header in `STANDARD.md` or the document set in `docs/index.json` changes | reflect the new version and updated counts/listings automatically across generated pages, with no hardcoded values |
| 3 | a generated page references CSS, JS, favicon, or another internal route | resolve to an existing file inside `_site/` via a relative path (no root-relative `/assets/…` paths that break under a GitHub Pages subpath) |
| 4 | any HTML page is emitted | contain exactly one `<h1>`, `<title>`, `<meta name="description">`, and `lang="pt-BR"` |
| 5 | prose or table cells mention an existing `ADR-NNNN` or `SPEC-NNNN` in the graph (outside code blocks) | convert the reference into a link to the corresponding document's generated page |
| 6 | an ADR has `status: superseded` or is referenced by other docs via `builds-on` | display the `VERDADE ATUAL` / `superseded-by` callout at the top and list reverse connections (`cited by` / `citado por`) on the document page |
| 7 | global search (`⌘K` / `/`) or graph filter matches zero items | display an explicit empty state with a clear-search/reset-filters button that restores the listing (ADR-0014) |
| 8 | the user toggles light/dark theme or clicks copy on a code/quickstart block | persist and apply `data-theme` without reloading the page and announce visual feedback on the copy button |
| 9 | `scripts/build-site` runs twice with no source changes | produce a byte-for-byte identical `_site/` tree (determinism) |
| 10 | `scripts/casa-init` runs against an adopting repository | never copy `scripts/build-site`, `scripts/test-site`, or `site/` into the target |
| 11 | `scripts/build-site` generates `_site/` at the root of `casa-standard` | keep `python3 scripts/docs-check` exiting 0 with 0 errors and 0 warnings (`_site/` ignored by `.gitignore`) |

## Open questions

(none — spec arrives decided)

## Definition of Done

```bash
scripts/test-site             # exit 0 — cases 1–11
scripts/test-casa-init        # exit 0 — bootstrap regression (case 10)
python3 scripts/docs-check    # exit 0 — this repository stays green (case 11)
```

## Human review

- Editorial readability across light and dark themes on desktop and mobile, free of visual clichés.
- Intuitive navigation between `STANDARD.md`, the `casa-*` skills, and the ADR/Spec graph nodes.

## Verification

```text
python3 scripts/docs-check    → 28 docs · 0 error(s) · 0 warning(s), exit 0 (--check-adr-immutability --base-ref origin/main and --staged)
bash scripts/test-docs-check  → 52 PASS / 0 FAIL · scripts/test-docs-reserve → 23 PASS / 0 FAIL · scripts/test-update-check → 14 PASS / 0 FAIL · scripts/test-install → 13 PASS / 0 FAIL
```
